newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks jump on election day, Telkom.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks jump on election day, Telkom.

text.p: Jakarta stocks rose sharply on Thursday, Indonesia's election day, on heavy buying in blue chip counters led by heavyweight Telkom, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 17 points, or 2.53 percent, to close at 689.50 points. Gainers led losers by 121 to 21, with 46 counters unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 784.3 billion rupiah, compared with 424 billion rupiah on Wednesday.
"The sharp rise in Telkom and other blue chip stocks really dragged up the index today," a broker with a Singaporean firm said.
Telkom accounts for about 16 percent of the weighting on the Jakarta composite index, brokers said.
Local brokers also said local investors had regained their confidence after the elections passed off without incident, particularly in Jakarta. Violence in East Timor did not affect sentiment.
Telkom closed 150 rupiah higher at 4,050 rupiah on a volume of 5.7 million shares and was cross-traded at a price of 4,075 rupiah on a volume of 26.5 million shares.
"Telkom rose sharply on intense market talk that it will do a private placement after previous rumours that Singapore Telecom had bought a stake in the firm," said a broker with foreign firm.

"From the company's side, we have no plan to sell a stake to Singapore Telecom," Thomas Widjanarto, head of Telkom's investor relations unit, told Reuters. Telkom is due to announce its first quarter results on Friday at 0400 GMT.
Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) declined comment on the rumours that it was taking a stake in Telkom.
"We do not comment on rumour and speculation," a SingTel spokeswoman told Reuters.
Some brokers believed widespread buying in blue chip stocks, especially in state-owned companies, was also supported by the government.
"I believe the government has an interest in creating a good image of investor confidence in the Indonesian bourse, especially on election day," a broker with a Malaysian firm said.
Brokers said domestic investors had shown speculative interest in some small stocks such as Bayu Buana and Mas Murni.

Property firm Mas Murni was active on talk it might sell a stake through a tender at a price of 1,200 rupiah. It was the most active stock during the day, rising 175 rupiah to 1,125 rupiah on 31.3 million shares.
Small tourism firm Bayu Buana was also active. "There was a rumour spreading in the market that it will acquire some star-rated hotels," a local broker said.
Company officials were not available for comment.
Brokers anticipated the index would advance further on Friday as more investors were expected to re-enter the market after the completion of the general elections.
Brokers said that toll road operator Citra Marga Nusaphala, which confirmed on Thursday it was planning a rights issue soon, was among several counters targetted for buying.
Others included Bank Negara Indonesia, Semen Gresik, Gudang Garam and Indofood.
